html:
Mecklenburg-Schwerin was a small German duchy on the Baltic coast, ruled from Schwerin. It was formed in 1701, when the old duchy of Mecklenburg was split between two branches of its ruling family; the smaller part became Mecklenburg-Strelitz.

It was a land of large estates, grain and old port towns such as Rostock and Wismar, which had been members of the Hanseatic League. Wismar was held by Sweden until 1803, when Sweden pledged it to Mecklenburg.

The duke joined Napoleon's Confederation of the Rhine in 1808 and was among the first German princes to leave it in 1813. The Congress of Vienna made him a grand duke. Mecklenburg kept an old system of rule by its landed nobles longer than most German states. It joined the German Empire in 1871 and became a free state in 1918.
